llm.summary: This documentation-only toolkit is coherent, but it recommends broad unattended agent permissions and remote wallet controls that can move funds before safeguards are configured.

dimensions.detail: For an agent-development toolkit, browser automation and wallet APIs are expected, but unrestricted outbound fetch plus local file mutation guidance and high-impact financial APIs need tighter scoping and explicit approval defaults.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Install instructions use unpinned global npm, unversioned ClawHub install/update, and mutable git clone commands; this is a supply-chain hygiene issue, not evidence of malicious install behavior in the artifact itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The agent-development rules recommend broad Write/Edit/Bash access and WebFetch(domain:*) in .claude/settings.json to avoid prompts, which can persistently expand generated agents beyond least privilege.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No cron, service, backdoor, or hidden persistence was found, but the artifact recommends persistent shell and .claude/settings.json changes that affect future sessions and agents.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The bundle purpose matches agent building, browser automation, wallet use, development, and docs, but the wallet guide includes server-side private-key custody, bearer-token transaction authority, swaps, transfers, arbitrary calldata, and a fail-open policy statement that all actions are allowed until policies are set.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. Use the wallet component only with empty or testnet wallets until the owner has claimed the wallet and configured strict spending, address, token, function, and approval policies. Do not grant generated agents blanket Write/Edit/Bash/WebFetch permissions; use narrow per-agent tool and domain allowlists instead. Prefer pinned installation versions and avoid placing API keys, platform credentials, or wallet bearer tokens in prompts, files, shell history, or logs.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Supported: the cited custom-agent instructions explicitly recommend prompt-free Write/Edit, broad Bash file commands, and WebFetch(domain:*) in agent settings.
[T09] unexpected: Supported as a material Review concern: wallet functionality is purpose-aligned, but fail-open policies, arbitrary transactions, remote custody, and bearer-token authority are under-controlled for moving assets.
[T08] expected: Partly supported as supply-chain risk from unpinned install commands; it does not by itself show malicious behavior.
[AS1] unexpected: Supported in context: the rule targets .claude/settings.json and recommends broad persistent allowlists, which is overbroad even for agent-authoring guidance.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Supported for wallet and financial automation examples: refunds, trading, transfers, swaps, and arbitrary contract calls are presented without strong default human-approval or fail-closed requirements.
[PE3] unexpected: Partly supported: the publishing example uses local credential and token arguments for platform connections without clear secret-storage warnings.
[P1] expected: Downgraded: the 'Ignore previous instructions' text appears inside a security-hardening example warning about prompt injection, not as an operative hidden instruction.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded for the same reason: the hidden HTML example is defensive documentation evidence, not an exploit instruction for the skill to follow.
[AS3] expected: Downgraded: the top-level SKILL.md lists bundled documentation paths; it does not instruct the agent to enumerate unrelated installed peer skills.
[E1] expected: Downgraded: the Anthropic API fetch appears as an anti-pattern that the guidance tells users to avoid.
[RA2] expected: Downgraded in part: dependency-copy commands are packaging notes, but persistent ~/.bashrc and .claude/settings.json changes remain user-visible privilege/persistence guidance concerns.
[SQP-1] expected: Partly supported: broad auto-trigger examples can cause over-delegation, but this is secondary to the wallet and permission-scope concerns.
